article_sentences: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links.

Hyderabad police intensified security across the city after receiving an email threatening bomb blasts at two prominent locations – Hotel Tourist Plaza in Kacheguda and Kacheguda Railway Station – and warning of a 26/11-style terror attack.
Although officials suspect the message to be a hoax, security arrangements have been tightened as a precaution.
The threat email, received on November 21, was reportedly sent by a person claiming links to the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT).
The sender allegedly threatened to target the hotel and railway station, claiming the attacks would kill at least 300 people.
Responding to the email, Telangana Director General of Police (DGP) CV Anand said that the prima facie evidence pointed to the mail being fake.
He however also said that officials are following Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) regarding the issue.

The email had also threatened to replicate the November 26, 2008, Mumbai terror attacks in Hyderabad to avenge the killing of LeT operative Lateef Bhat and his associates by the Indian Army in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir.

Following the alert issued by the Special Branch, police personnel across Hyderabad were directed to strengthen security at the two locations and step up surveillance at crowded public spaces, including hotels, railway stations, bus stations, religious places and other key installations.
Anti-sabotage checks were carried out at the locations named in the email and other sensitive areas.
Police said no explosives were found during the searches.
Patrolling and visible policing have also been increased, while personnel have been instructed to watch out for suspicious individuals, unattended objects and vehicles.

stories.headline: St Theressa Institute students visit Usman War Memorial along LoC
stories.title: St Theressa Institute students visit Usman War Memorial along LoC
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 22: Jhangar Battalion of the Indian Army organised an educational visit for around 200 students of St Theressa Institute of Education, Rajouri, to the Usman War Memorial located along the Line of Control (LoC). The visit aimed at familiarising students with the military history of the region and inspiring them through the courage, leadership and sacrifices of soldiers who defended the nation. During the visit, students were briefed about the “Battle of Nowshera”, fought during the 1947-48 Indo-Pak conflict. They were informed about the challenging circumstances faced by the Indian Army and the determined resistance offered by troops to defend Nowshera and adjoining areas. Special emphasis was laid on the role of Brigadier Mohammad Usman, popularly known as the 'Lion of Nowshera'. Students were apprised of his exemplary leadership, courage and ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty while defending the strategic Nowshera sector. They were also briefed about the historical significance of the Usman War Memorial and the importance of preserving the legacy of soldiers who laid down their lives in the service of the nation. The interaction highlighted values of discipline, courage, perseverance, leadership and selfless service, while encouraging students to learn from history and become responsible citizens. Organised under the theme 'Know Your History, Be Inspired for Tomorrow', the initiative provided students an opportunity to experience history beyond textbooks and develop a deeper understanding of the sacrifices made by the Armed Forces. “The visit was part of Jhangar Battalion's continued efforts to connect with the local community, promote awareness about the region's military heritage and inspire younger generations through stories of valour and sacrifice,” the Army spokesperson said.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan disrupts fishing in Tamil Nadu's Tuticorin; fishermen seek Rs 5,000 assistance
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan disrupts fishing in Tamil Nadu's Tuticorin; fishermen seek Rs 5,000 assistance
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu): Over 200 mechanised fishing boats from Tuticorin ventured into the sea early on Monday after a 10-day break triggered by Cyclone Akvan, even as fishermen urged the Tamil Nadu government to provide Rs 5,000 in relief to tide over the monsoon-induced lean period.
Following an India Meteorological Department warning of strong winds over the sea due to Cyclone Akvan, the Tuticorin district.
Fisheries Department had barred fishermen from venturing into the waters from November 13 until further notice.
After the restriction was lifted, country-boat and fibre-boat fishermen resumed operations on November 20.
Mechanised boat operators, however, remained ashore for 10 days before setting sail early Monday from the Tuticorin Mechanised Boat Fishing Harbour.
With fishing resuming after a 10-day gap, fishermen expressed optimism that the catch would be good.
Highlighting the recurring impact of the northeast monsoon, fishermen noted that rough seas and cyclonic systems between October and December steadily reduce their working days every year.
In November alone, they were forced to stay off the sea for 17 days, severely affecting their livelihoods.

Fishermen urged the state government to enhance the financial assistance extended during the May fishing ban and lean fishing periods, and provide an additional Rs 5,000 to cover the three-month monsoon lean season.

A fishermen's representative told PTI Videos that it has become extremely difficult to venture into the sea even for 150 days out of 365 in a year, given cyclones, floods, and the mandatory 60-day annual fishing ban.

Urging the government to intervene and hike the relief amount this year itself, the representative sought an immediate allocation of Rs 5,000 for the November–December period to support families facing severe hardship.
Tuticorin is a major fishing harbour, with over 20,000 people depending directly on the sector and another 10,000 indirectly for their livelihoods.

stories.headline: CPI(M) Accuses BJP of Violating Tripura Poll Rules Over Election Pamphlets, Posters
stories.title: CPI(M) Accuses BJP of Violating Tripura Poll Rules Over Election Pamphlets, Posters
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: AGARTALA: The CPI(M) has alleged that the ruling BJP is violating the election code of conduct and urged the State Election Commission to take appropriate action.

The party claimed that the pamphlets and posters being used by the BJP for its election campaign did not carry the mandatory declaration of the printer and publisher, as required under the Tripura Municipal (Conduct of Election) Rules, 1995.
The complaint was filed by CPI(M) state secretary Jitendra Chaudhury, who demanded an immediate halt to the distribution of the pamphlets and legal action against the concerned printer and publisher.
According to the complaint, BJP workers had been distributing the pamphlets door-to-door while campaigning in various municipal and nagar panchayat areas ahead of the November 27 polls.

The pamphlets reportedly carried photographs and appeals from Chief Minister Manik Saha, BJP state president Abhishek Debray and MP Biplab Kumar Deb, along with the party's election symbol and an appeal to vote for the BJP.
Chaudhury cited sub-rule (1) of Rule 95 of the 1995 rules, which bars the printing or publication of election material without the mandatory declaration.
He also alleged that several flexes, posters, hoardings and banners featuring BJP candidates across Agartala lacked the required details of the printer and publisher.
Citing sub-rule (4) of the same rule, Chaudhury said violations attracted imprisonment of up to six months, a fine of up to Rs 2,000, or both.
He called for strict enforcement of the election rules to ensure free and fair polls.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has credited citizens for responding to his appeal to avoid unnecessary gold purchases, as gold prices take a dip. Speaking at the National Skill Convocation in Lucknow, the PM said public cooperation could help conserve India's foreign exchange reserves amid global economic and energy uncertainties. The appeal, first made in Hyderabad in May, has also received backing from traders' bodies and Union Minister Piyush Goyal. But Modi's comparison with former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri's appeal to give up one meal a week during the 1965 war has triggered a political controversy, with Congress MP Imran Masood questioning the comparison. Did the appeal help India's economy, or has it become another political flashpoint?

article_sentences: The Supreme Court declined to hear a plea over the demolition of a century-old Saharanpur mosque.
It ruled that the jurisdictional high court must first examine any breach of demolition guidelines.

The Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear a plea alleging that the demolition of a 100-year-old mosque in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district violated its 2024 guidelines on demolitions involving bulldozers, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
The court asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional high court, saying alleged violations of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before it in every case.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea filed by Imran Ahmad against Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal.
The petition alleged non-compliance with the Supreme Court's directions.
Declining to examine the allegations directly, the Chief Justice said, "Every order violating a Supreme Court judgment cannot come back to the Supreme Court itself.
You have to go to the respective high court," according to Press Trust of India.
The bench said it would be necessary to examine the specific facts and circumstances of the demolition to determine whether the guidelines had been violated.
It said the jurisdictional high court was better placed to carry out this exercise.
"We have laid down the principles, but then wherever these principles have been violated, in what factual context and background?
Please go to the concerned high court, establish your case on facts, and if the high court doesn't grant you necessary relief, then come to us," the Chief Justice said.

stories.headline: The Book and the Belonging
stories.title: The Book and the Belonging
stories.summary: At the November 16, 2026 launch of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Mrs Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ in a five-star hotel in New Delhi, the presence of I.N.D.I.A bloc leaders alongside Congress figures and an odd newly baptised BJP leaders, projected multiple political and personal messages. Different political observers, parties, and commentators interpreted the event differently. However, despite Mrs Gandhi stressing the book - as the word ‘Belonging…’ reflected- is a personal account more focused on Nehru-Gandhi family, it could not escape creating a strong political imprint. The imprint was based on the opposition unity jigsaw which saw a fine-print unfolding in the shape of who-is-who of I.N.D.I.A bloc partners in attendance to give political strength to the function which the author and the organisers must have cherished. In fact, the political flavour dominated the social colouring which might or might not be to the liking of Mrs Gandhi. Samajwadi Party chief and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Mr Akhilesh Yadav sounded sanguine and amply conveyed the spirit and environment of the book release function in his thoughts, he penned down at the book launch. “Let us come together and write a book in which we write a revolution of change.” It was a political message obliquely hinting at the electoral battles, particularly coming Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, ahead. No doubt, he also wrote on the virtues of books and publishing but this observation conveyed the basic spirit and purpose behind lining up the I.N.D.I.A combine leadership. Ostensibly, a painstaking effort had gone into organising the function to its finer details right from the guest list to the sitting arrangement with entire focus on opposition unity. The plan seemed less on arrogance, as the allies have often accused the Congress of, and more on displaying a spirit of accommodation and dignity towards allies, mostly regional parties and much smaller in size, than the Grand Old Party (GOP) dominating the scene, as had been the practice in the past. In fact, it was in continuation of the Congress-planned framework seen during the last few programmes aimed at reflecting I.N.D.I.A groupings unity. This continuity is seen in the Opposition camps attempts at delivering message of bonding at short intervals so as not to give rivals any chance at talking about disunity and differences in the grouping’s ranks delaying their meeting. This bonding was reflected during the last two shows - the rally at the Ramlila Maidan over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the march to Supreme Court of India to file a joint petition, by the I.N.D.I.A partners in this regard. The show on Mrs Gandhi’s book launch was a powerful exhibition of the same spirit. The spotlight on the Opposition leaders became more nuanced in this function. The leaders such as Samajwadi party chief Mr Yadav and his MP wife Mrs Dimple Yadav, Jharkhand chief minister Mr Hemant Soren and his legislator wife Mrs Kalpana Soren, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Mr Omar Abdullah and his father and National Conference patriarch Dr Farooq Abdullah, Peoples Democratic Party chief Ms Mehbooba Mufti, Trinamool Congress leader Mr Abhishek Banerjee, MP (nephew of TMC chief Ms Mamta Banerjee), Tamil Nadu chief minister Mr C Joseph Vijay, Nationalist Congress Party (SP) leader and MP Ms Supriya Sule among others, were given the front-row privilege in the sitting arrangement. Mrs Sonia Gandhi on arrival sitting next to Mr Yadav before she shifted on to the stage for the book release, was a classic sight. It was certainly not difficult to relate it to early 2027 UP assembly elections. Presence of a Gandhi-family friend and former Punjab chief minister Captain Amrinder Singh, who is now a BJP leader, added an interesting political dimension to the function. His presence, in view of the coming Punjab assembly elections and speculations about return to Congress, added grist of a different kind to ongoing opposition unity efforts. Their presence turned a literary evening into a political occasion. But question arises: Can the warmth of one evening survive the demands of electoral politics given the fragile nature of opposition unity? No doubt the real test for this unity lies ahead for which further continuation of bonding efforts is necessary. Apart from Mrs Gandhi, the author of the book being the focus of the show, and Congress president Mr Mallikarjun Kharge occupying front row seat alongside Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Mr Rahul Gandhi, most of the party leaders including AICC general secretary Mrs Priyanka Gandhi along with her in-laws’ family occupied the second-row seats. This was a notable point in relation to Congress’s relations with its allies. On the face of it Congress gave an impression of playing a second fiddle to the alliance partners, mostly regional players. However, it seemed to be part of a well-thought of plan which has also been visible during the last few outings of the I.N.D.I.A bloc spearheaded and planned by the Congress. Mr had been the master of ceremonies in all the previous opposition bloc programmes. The limelight though was on Mrs Gandhi in the book launch function but he did make his mark in his role to make concluding remarks. His short address, which he began “under instructions of no political talk on the occasion” was passionate, impressive and calculated. It conveyed a strong message where it was meant to be sent. Notwithstanding claims of Mrs Gandhi about the book and related issues being of personal and social nature, the gathering as a show of opposition solidarity was certainly not without a political message. Coming ahead of upcoming state elections in states such as politically significant Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa and Manipur, and with Samajwadi Party- the bigger partner in Uttar Pradesh- chief Mr Yadav kept in prominence, and from Punjab perspective Captain Singh occupying the first row, the messaging was well crafted and strong. There is the other side to this opposition unity which the Congress has been in dire need to establish its credentials as I.N.D.I.A bloc leader. Clearly, it has been able to make its mark during the last three programmes with agitation over SIR (arbitrary deletion and addition of votes by the Election Commission) becoming the cementing force. Somewhere the book launch function has rekindled Congress’s hopes to strike the chemistry that had shaped the United Progressive Alliance (UPA)-1 in 2004. A personal Narrative and “Setting the Record Straight”! This was the premise and backdrop to which Mrs Gandhi had sought to set the narrative of the programme. She had clearly stated that the book was meant to share her own feelings and counter narratives and untruths written about her and her family. No doubt both the book and thoughts expressed during the launch function stuck to this plan. However, the collective spirit of the book launch function had been guided by a greater political aim. On both these counts the book launch proved productive.

stories.headline: High Court upholds 2.5 lakh penalty over energising fuel station without NoC
stories.title: High Court upholds 2.5 lakh penalty over energising fuel station without NoC
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 22: The High Court of J&K and Ladakh has upheld Rs 2.5 lakh penalty imposed on Indian Oil Corporation for energising a petrol pump in Pulwama district’s Lethpora without final access permission from the National Highway Administration. A bench of Justice Sanjay Dhar, while deciding a plea, however, directed the District Magistrate Pulwama, to conduct an inquiry into whether the petrol pump operated under the name of M/s Fatima Filling Station and if the same had been established at the sanctioned location after obtaining all requisite No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from the concerned departments. The Court also directed the district administration to remove encroachments, if any, on the land of the National Highway that are obstructing the construction of an access road to the petrol pump strictly in accordance with law. In a plea, the aggrieved petitioner had called in question a communication dated July 28, 2025, whereby the National Highway Authority (NHA) directed the Chief Manager, Retail Sales, Indian Oil Corporation, to deposit a penalty of Rs 2.5 lakh for energising the fuel station without obtaining the final NOC. The NHA also directed the Corporation to de-energise the retail outlet until the grant of final access permission. The petitioner’s argument was that the petrol pump was set up after obtaining necessary clearances under the Petroleum Act, 1934, and Petroleum Rules, 2002, besides securing provisional access permission from the NHA in 2021. Furthermore, the petitioner contended that the final access permission could not be obtained because of encroachments by local residents and shopkeepers on National Highway land, which, she claimed, the authorities had failed to remove despite repeated requests. In its response, the NHA, however, maintained that the petrol pump had been energised and commercial operations commenced without obtaining final access permission, in violation of the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways on June 26, 2020. Underscoring that the guidelines clearly prohibit energising a fuel station on the basis of provisional access permission and permit such operations only after grant of regular access permission, the court upheld the penalty. It noted that without constructing the access to the petrol pump, the same could not be energized in any circumstances whatsoever. The Court, however, recorded that the petitioner had been unable to construct the access road as neither the NHA nor the district administration had succeeded in removing the encroachments. These circumstances, it said, could provide justification for seeking an extension of provisional access permission and additional time for construction of the approach road, but could not justify operating the petrol pump without final permission. The Court observed that the encroachments were required to be removed in accordance with the provisions of the Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002. The District Magistrate was vested with powers under Sections 26, 27, 36 and 43 of the Act to facilitate swift removal of encroachments on National Highway land, the court said. The Court held that the District Magistrate, Pulwama in keeping with the Supreme Court's directions in Gyan Prakash vs Union of India, was duty-bound to ensure removal of all encroachments obstructing construction of the access to the petrol pump. The bench directed the District Magistrate to hold an inquiry and if it was established that the petitioner had fulfilled all statutory requirements and obtained the requisite NOCs, she should be allowed to operate the petrol pump at the sanctioned location. Thereafter, upon construction of the access road, the NHA shall grant the necessary final access permission and allow energisation of the outlet, it said. The Court, however, ordered that if any deficiencies were found, the petitioner should be given an opportunity to rectify those, failing which the petrol pump be closed down or sealed.

article_sentences: Indore Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri has said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s policies insulated Indian consumers from global fuel price shocks, underscoring that domestic retail prices remained largely stable despite international crises.

Inspecting petrol pumps in Indore on Sunday, the Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh said the Centre had cut excise duty three times, in November 2021, May 2022 and March 10, 2026, limiting the rise in fuel prices in India to "around seven per cent against a 50-70 per cent surge globally".
PM Modi's policies protected Indians from global fuel price shocks, he told reporters.

He also praised state-run oil marketing companies Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) for "absorbing heavy losses" when crude oil prices rose from $60-65 to $120 per barrel.

stories.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 22: Food regulator FSSAI on Sunday said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after finding its sample of packaged drinking water "unsafe". In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water". A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis. "The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said. Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added. The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law. Hence, the FSSAI said it has granted sanction to launch prosecution under the FSS Act, 2006, against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd. During this calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators as well as e-commerce companies. The regulator has also cracked down on energy drink and alcoholic beverage makers.

opening: Nepal PM Balen Shah's India visit, which includes a keenly-watched official talk with Narendra Modi on November 23, comes at a crucial juncture for both countries.
With a new govt in Nepal and the country in need of major reconstruction projects in the wake of the devastating recent floods, the ambit of the talks this time is bigger than usual.
body: Not just politics, the agenda also covers trade expansion, hydropower investments, cross-border connectivity, digital payments and infrastructure projects.

Also read | India-EU trade deal likely to be signed on December 16From a well-set bilateral electricity trade to Nepal's reliance on India for export transits, the two sides' interdependence has been deep.
Over the past few years, digital payments have added another aspect to bilateral dealings.
Modi-Shah talks could take this interdependence to a new level.
Indian power, infrastructure, logistics and technology companies could be looking at a new beginning in Nepal as the two sides go about deepening trade ties further.
Trade ties: The story so farIndian businesses have for some time been looking forward to more opportunities to transform good neighbourly ties into bankable projects in Nepal.
India is already Nepal’s largest trading and investment partner.
Bilateral merchandise trade reached $9.38 billion in FY26, accounting for more than 60% of Nepal’s external goods trade.
It is the largest source of foreign investment in Nepal, with Indian investments estimated at around $800 million across nearly 150 ventures.
Banking, insurance, telecommunications, power, education and tourism are among the sectors attracting Indian capital.
The challenge now is to make this relationship more balanced by encouraging Nepalese exports, expanding investment flows and widening opportunities for businesses on both sides.
Power playPower sector could offer one of the biggest opportunities.
Nepal has considerable hydropower potential, while India has a huge electricity market.
The long-term power trade agreement envisages India buying up to 10,000 MW of electricity from Nepal over 10 years.
India has another major factor going for it -- the transmission infrastructure needed to connect producers with consumers.
India currently imports around 1,200 MW from Nepal.
Indian companies, including PSU ones, have major interests in developing hydropower projects in Nepal.
Faster project clearances, predictable regulatory approvals, transmission-line investments and assured market access would help speed up these investments, an ET report said citing experts.
Also read | Asia, Africa to drive expansion of India's export markets as shipments grow across regions.
The two governments can also explore greater private-sector participation in generation, storage and grid infrastructure, Reuters reported in September.
The destruction of Nepal's power infra in the floods has put electricity trade more in focus.
India approved electricity exports of up to 654 MW to Nepal for 18 hours daily until December 31, 2026.
The deal made clear the value of an integrated regional electricity market, Reuters reported.
Other than supplying to India, Nepal also exports its power to Bangladesh through India's transmission network.
This transmission has been a critical part of efforts to establish a model for a wider regional energy business.
Close connectExporters from the land-locked Nepal are heavily dependent on India for access to the seas.
Connectivity is another major area where Indian infra companies stand to benefit from closer ties.
Kolkata, Haldia and Visakhapatnam ports are important gateways for its third-country trade.
Any disruption along these routes can have huge impact on Nepal's supplies and businesses.
The new direct commercial freight train service connecting Kolkata Port with Biratnagar Customs Yard is a step towards reducing transit time, cargo handling and logistics costs.
Border congestion, customs procedures and infrastructure gaps continue to hinder trade for Nepal, said an ET report.
Shah's visit is an opportunity to push for faster customs clearance, integrated check posts, better warehousing and more efficient rail-road connections, it added.
A digital bridgeDigital connectivity offer another promising opening to both sides.
The UPI-National Payments Interface linkage, operationalised in June 2026, enables real-time person-to-person transfers between the two countries.
The earlier QR-based merchant payment arrangement has also made transactions easier for Indian visitors in Nepal.
Expanding these facilities to cover more banks, merchants and businesses could strengthen tourism, retail commerce and help small entrepreneurs.
Cooperation in fintech, digital public infrastructure and technology services could create opportunities for Indian technology companies while making cross-border commerce smoother, ET reported.
Infra & other avenues.
There could emerge many new opportunities in the areas of manufacturing, tourism, agriculture and green energy as well, besides in climate-resilient infra.
Indian companies could get projects in rebuilding of roads, bridges and power facilities damaged by floods.
They also might get new opportunities for investing in industrial parks, food processing, transmission networks and logistics infrastructure.

Revisiting the bilateral trade treaty to address investment protection, market access and smoother movement of goods could further improve the business environment, ET had reported earlier quoting a number of trade analysts.
For Indian companies, the size of the opportunity will be decided by policy predictability in Nepal and timely clearances by its govt.
The commercial viability of these projects would be another big decider.
Nepal, for its part, is aiming for higher value addition, more jobs and a better diversified export economy.
It is also seeking a more equal share in the bilateral trade equation -- currently dominated by imports from India.
